The projection preserves polynomial size and constant depth; ACC0 retains its fixed modulus set. No uniform generator for the original NC1 family is required.

hardwiring_proof.source_language: Well-formed true variable-free Boolean formulas in parenthesized fixed-width binary syntax
steps: BFV belongs to ALOGTIME by Buss MainTheorem1; fixed-width binary coding is explicit in §2.
Unfold each bounded-fan-in logarithmic-depth nonuniform circuit into a polynomial-size formula.
Replace leaf variables by their bits using equal-width 0/1 tokens. The resulting formula has length depending only on n, and each encoded bit is a constant or input literal.
Restrict the target-class BFV circuit at that length. Constant depth and polynomial size are preserved; ACC0 introduces no new moduli.
scope_guards: No uniform generation of the original nonuniform NC1 family is required.
Do not replace the parenthesized syntax by a pointer-table formula representation.
Derived mathematical rule, not a kernel-checked circuit-simulation theorem.

family_reviews.review: Four small focus classes are in P, so their outward counting inclusions are inherited. ∃R versus CH/PSharpP/PP remains candidate where not already implied; no PosSLP-to-entire-class transfer.
The small four are below P. Seven surviving large-resource candidates involve ExistsR; PSPACE upper bounds do not settle those directions.
Use the explicit L/UL/NL/PL and UniformNC1 chains; do not silently add BPL↔UL or PL↔BPL.

All five focus endpoints are in PSPACE. Arbitrary unary languages witness the thirty incoming nonuniform exclusions; parity gives five outgoing AC0 exclusions. The two new conditional rules do not change baseline statuses.
Check PL/LogCFL/SC in both directions; NC² does not imply simultaneous SC, AC¹ is not SAC¹, and polynomial-clocked BQL does not inherit postselection.
Use P for small focus classes, NP⊆ExistsR and complement propagation as applicable. Real-valued PCPs and complex feasibility theorems do not give binary proof-class bounds for real feasibility.
Review BPL⊆BQL⊆PL directly. StrongFewL is not ordinary UL; postselection is not BQL. Quantum amplitudes do not yield a polynomial-size real-feasibility encoding for general witnesses.

The strongest remaining omission risks are PL/SC/LogCFL, ordinary unambiguity versus randomized/quantum logspace, and ExistsR versus counting/proof classes.
